subproblems.title: Countable open cover with Lipschitz pieces for a map locally Lipschitz on an arbitrary set (parent step 1)
subproblems.statement: For all P, Q ∈ ℕ, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P and every map f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q that is locally Lipschitz on U, there are open sets O_i ⊆ ℝ^P and constants K_i ∈ ℝ≥0 (i ∈ ℕ) such that U ⊆ ⋃_i O_i and f is K_i-Lipschitz on O_i ∩ U for every i. Here 'locally Lipschitz on U' means: every x ∈ U has a neighbourhood t within U (t ∈ 𝓝[U] x) and a constant K ≥ 0 such that f is K-Lipschitz on t.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q), LocallyLipschitzOn U f → ∃ (O : ℕ → Set (Eucl P)) (K : ℕ → ℝ≥0), (∀ i, IsOpen (O i)) ∧ U ⊆ ⋃ i, O i ∧ ∀ i, LipschitzOnWith (K i) f (O i ∩ U)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). `LocallyLipschitzOn U f` means: for every x ∈ U there are K ∈ ℝ≥0 and a set t ∈ 𝓝[U] x (a neighbourhood of x within U) such that f is K-Lipschitz on t (`LipschitzOnWith K f t`: edist (f y) (f z) ≤ K · edist y z for all y, z ∈ t). Being K-Lipschitz on a set passes to its subsets (`LipschitzOnWith.mono`), and every map is 0-Lipschitz on ∅ (`lipschitzOnWith_empty`). This is step 2 (countable Lipschitz cover) of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary set U with pieces O_i ∩ U. Its frozen Lean type is byte-identical to the already comparator-accepted declaration Submission.lpf_lli_countable_lipschitz_cover, which is reused rather than re-proved. The parent applies it with U := Ω and f := u.

1. (Local open pieces.) Fix x ∈ U and choose K_x ∈ ℝ≥0 and t_x ∈ 𝓝[U] x with f K_x-Lipschitz on t_x. A set belongs to 𝓝[U] x iff it contains O ∩ U for some open O ∋ x (Mathlib `mem_nhdsWithin`). So there is an open O_x ⊆ ℝ^P with x ∈ O_x and O_x ∩ U ⊆ t_x, and f is K_x-Lipschitz on O_x ∩ U by monotonicity. For x ∉ U put O_x := ∅ and K_x := 0, so x ↦ O_x is a total function. These values are never used: the Lindelöf step below only involves O_x for x ∈ U, and every point it returns lies in U.

2. (Lindelöf.) ℝ^P is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelöf, so every subset of ℝ^P, in particular U, is Lindelöf (Mathlib instance `SecondCountableTopology.toHereditarilyLindelof`, lemma `HereditarilyLindelofSpace.isLindelof U`). For x ∈ U the open set O_x contains x, so O_x ∈ 𝓝 x and hence O_x ∈ 𝓝[U] x. The neighbourhood form of the Lindelöf property gives a countable set T ⊆ U with U ⊆ ⋃_{x ∈ T} O_x. In Mathlib this is `IsLindelof.elim_nhds_subcover`, or directly `TopologicalSpace.countable_cover_nhdsWithin` applied to x ↦ O_x, the tool used in the parent's step 2.

3. (Case T = ∅.) Then U ⊆ ⋃_{x ∈ ∅} O_x = ∅, so U = ∅. Take O_i := ∅ and K_i := 0 for every i ∈ ℕ. Each O_i is open, U = ∅ ⊆ ⋃_i O_i, and f is 0-Lipschitz on O_i ∩ U = ∅.

4. (Case T ≠ ∅.) A nonempty countable set is the range of a sequence (Mathlib `Set.Countable.exists_eq_range`), so T = {g(i) : i ∈ ℕ} for some g : ℕ → ℝ^P. Put O_i := O_{g(i)} and K_i := K_{g(i)}. Since g(i) ∈ T ⊆ U, step 1 shows that O_i is open and f is K_i-Lipschitz on O_i ∩ U for every i.

5. (Cover.) Let x ∈ U. By step 2 there is y ∈ T with x ∈ O_y, and y = g(i) for some i ∈ ℕ, so x ∈ O_{g(i)} = O_i. Hence U ⊆ ⋃_i O_i. Together with step 4 (or step 3 when T = ∅) this proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: For each x ∈ U choose K_x and an open O_x ∋ x with O_x ∩ U ⊆ t_x (mem_nhdsWithin), so f is K_x-Lipschitz on O_x ∩ U.
ℝ^P is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelöf, so some countable T ⊆ U has U ⊆ ⋃_{x∈T} O_x (IsLindelof.elim_nhds_subcover or TopologicalSpace.countable_cover_nhdsWithin).
If T = ∅ then U = ∅, and O_i = ∅, K_i = 0 work.
Otherwise T = range g (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range); put O_i := O_{g(i)} (open) and K_i := K_{g(i)}. Then f is K_i-Lipschitz on O_i ∩ U and U ⊆ ⋃_i O_i.

subproblems.title: Countable partition of a null-measurable D ⊆ Ω into disjoint null-measurable pieces inside open sets on which a locally Lipschitz map is Lipschitz
subproblems.statement: Let n, Q ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q locally Lipschitz on Ω, and D ⊆ Ω Lⁿ-null-measurable. Then there are sets V_m, B_m ⊆ ℝⁿ and constants K_m ∈ ℝ≥0 (m ∈ ℕ) such that every V_m is open, V_m ⊆ Ω, u is K_m-Lipschitz on V_m, B_m ⊆ D ∩ V_m, the B_m are pairwise disjoint, every B_m is Lⁿ-null-measurable, and D ⊆ ⋃_m B_m.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n Q : ℕ) (Ω D : Set (Eucl n)) (u : Eucl n → Eucl Q), IsOpen Ω → LocallyLipschitzOn Ω u → D ⊆ Ω → NullMeasurableSet D (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) → ∃ (V B : ℕ → Set (Eucl n)) (K : ℕ → ℝ≥0), (∀ m, IsOpen (V m)) ∧ (∀ m, V m ⊆ Ω) ∧ (∀ m, LipschitzOnWith (K m) u (V m)) ∧ (∀ m, B m ⊆ D ∩ V m) ∧ Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint B) ∧ (∀ m, NullMeasurableSet (B m) (volume : Measure (Eucl n))) ∧ D ⊆ ⋃ m, B m
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝⁿ = Eucl n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), and Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ. `LocallyLipschitzOn Ω u` means: every x ∈ Ω has K ∈ ℝ≥0 and a set t ∈ 𝓝[Ω] x on which u is K-Lipschitz. For a sequence of sets V, `disjointed V m` = V m \ ⋃_{l<m} V l (Mathlib `disjointed`). Hypotheses: Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, u locally Lipschitz on Ω, D ⊆ Ω, D Lⁿ-null-measurable. This is steps 2–3 of the parent proof (countable Lipschitz cover and disjoint pieces). It is import-free: everything used is in the frozen import closure of GMT.Ch06.Submission plus the sibling countable_lipschitz_cover.

1. (Countable Lipschitz cover.) Apply the sibling theorem countable_lipschitz_cover (Submission.lpf_lli_countable_lipschitz_cover) with P := n, Q := Q, U := Ω, f := u. It gives open sets O_m ⊆ ℝⁿ and constants K_m ∈ ℝ≥0 (m ∈ ℕ) with Ω ⊆ ⋃_m O_m and u K_m-Lipschitz on O_m ∩ Ω for every m.

2. (Open Lipschitz pieces inside Ω.) Put V_m := O_m ∩ Ω.
   - V_m is open, as the intersection of two open sets (IsOpen.inter).
   - V_m ⊆ Ω.
   - u is K_m-Lipschitz on V_m by step 1.
   - Ω ⊆ ⋃_m V_m: if x ∈ Ω, then x ∈ O_m for some m by step 1, so x ∈ O_m ∩ Ω = V_m.

3. (Disjointification.) Let W_m := disjointed V m. By Mathlib:
   - W_m ⊆ V_m (disjointed_subset);
   - the W_m are pairwise disjoint (disjoint_disjointed);
   - each W_m is measurable (MeasurableSet.disjointed, since each V_m is open and hence Borel measurable);
   - ⋃_m W_m = ⋃_m V_m (iUnion_disjointed).

4. (Pieces.) Put B_m := D ∩ W_m.
   (a) B_m ⊆ D ∩ V_m, because W_m ⊆ V_m (Set.inter_subset_inter_right).
   (b) For i ≠ j, B_i and B_j are disjoint, since B_i ⊆ W_i, B_j ⊆ W_j and W_i, W_j are disjoint (Disjoint.mono).
   (c) Each B_m is Lⁿ-null-measurable: it is the intersection of the null-measurable set D with the measurable set W_m (NullMeasurableSet.inter with MeasurableSet.nullMeasurableSet).
   (d) D ⊆ ⋃_m B_m. Let x ∈ D. Then x ∈ Ω ⊆ ⋃_m V_m = ⋃_m W_m by steps 2 and 3, so x ∈ W_m for some m, and hence x ∈ D ∩ W_m = B_m.

5. (Conclusion.) The sequences V, B and K satisfy every conclusion. V_m is open, V_m ⊆ Ω and u is K_m-Lipschitz on V_m (step 2). Moreover B_m ⊆ D ∩ V_m, the B_m are pairwise disjoint, every B_m is Lⁿ-null-measurable, and D ⊆ ⋃_m B_m (step 4). ∎
proof_key_steps: Apply countable_lipschitz_cover (lpf_lli_countable_lipschitz_cover) to U := Ω, f := u: open O_m and K_m with Ω ⊆ ⋃ O_m and u K_m-Lipschitz on O_m ∩ Ω.
V_m := O_m ∩ Ω is open, V_m ⊆ Ω, u is K_m-Lipschitz on V_m, and Ω ⊆ ⋃ V_m.
W_m := disjointed V m: measurable, pairwise disjoint, W_m ⊆ V_m and ⋃ W_m = ⋃ V_m (MeasurableSet.disjointed, disjoint_disjointed, disjointed_subset, iUnion_disjointed).
B_m := D ∩ W_m is contained in D ∩ V_m, pairwise disjoint and null-measurable, and D ⊆ Ω ⊆ ⋃ W_m gives D ⊆ ⋃ B_m.
